rules.title: RevenueDot Unity SDK
rules.description: RevenueDot's MIT fork of RevenueCat's Unity SDK, pointed at RevenueDot, the open-source RevenueCat alternative for in-app purchases and subscriptions.
rules: Install with `openupm add com.revenuedot.purchases-unity`, or from the git URL https://github.com/revenuedot/purchases-unity.git?path=RevenueCat in the Unity Package Manager.
C# namespaces and assembly names are unchanged, so `using RevenueCat;` keeps working.
RevenueDot Cloud ({{apiHost}}) is the default API host. For a self-hosted server, fill the Purchases component's Proxy URL field.
Pass the app's public key from the RevenueDot dashboard to `Purchases.PurchasesConfiguration.Builder.Init`: appl_ for iOS and goog_ for Android.

rules.title: RevenueDot Unity SDK
install: Or **Window > Package Manager > + > Add package from git URL**:

C# namespaces and assembly names are unchanged, so `using RevenueCat;` keeps working. The External Dependency Manager pulls the native side: the `RevenueDotPurchasesHybridCommon` pod and `{{mavenGroup}}:purchases-hybrid-common`.

code: // On the Purchases component tick "Use Runtime Setup". Self-hosted server only: RevenueDot Cloud ({{apiHost}}) is the default.
// For a self-hosted server, fill the component's Proxy URL field. Then, in a script that runs after Purchases.Start():
purchases.Configure(Purchases.PurchasesConfiguration.Builder.Init("appl_...").Build());   // the app's public key from the RevenueDot dashboard

checks.run: for f in RevenueCat/Plugins/Editor/RevenueCatDependencies.xml RevenueCatUI/Plugins/Editor/RevenueCatUIDependencies.xml; do xmllint --noout "$f" && echo "$f ok" || exit 1; done
